description: A systems administrator manually modified access logs to conceal his presence on the server the night before confidential data disappeared. VIGÍA must detect the temporal inconsistencies and evidence of manual editing.
analyst_notes: Classic insider threat case. The forensic difficulty is that the attacker has legitimate access — only the technical details reveal the manipulation.

forensic_anomalies: The file was modified at 23:47 on April 10 according to the filesystem inode — hours after the last recorded entry
The 08:45 and 17:30 entries have second-level precision but the kernel log shows microsecond gaps inconsistent with real logging
The usual sudo and cron entries that appear on every other day of the month are missing
PID 2891 at 17:30 is numerically lower than PID 2934 recorded at 16:15 in another log — PIDs cannot decrease

content.editor_signature: VIM — Last modified indicator present in file slack space

forensic_anomalies: inode mtime 23:47 — the log was touched nearly 6 hours after the last recorded entry (17:38)
VIM signature in file slack space confirms manual editing with a text editor — system logs are NEVER edited with vim
access time == modify time — indicates the attacker did not read the file before modifying it, directly overwrote it
Owner is 'syslog' but vim requires elevated permissions to write — the editor was run as root

artifacts.source: NetFlow — core switch, HR server port
forensic_anomalies: Two SSH connections at 23:41 and 23:47 that do NOT appear in auth.log — these are exactly the deleted sessions
First session (23:41): 2.1MB transferred in 84 seconds — consistent with HR database exfiltration
Second session (23:47): only 64 bytes in 17 seconds — enough time to run vim and save the modified log
10.0.0.15 is the workstation IP of Carlos M., a systems administrator with authorized overnight access

ground_truth.real_damage: 847 employee records exfiltrated including banking data
ground_truth.cover_up_method: manual editing of auth.log with vim to remove nighttime sessions

mitre_actual.T1070.002: Clear Linux or Mac System Logs — manual editing of auth.log
mitre_actual.T1078.001: Default Accounts — use of own administrator credentials
mitre_actual.T1565.001: Stored Data Manipulation — on-disk log modification

peirce_expected.firstness: Apparently normal access log with sessions during business hours. No surface-level alerts.
peirce_expected.secondness: NetFlow shows two nighttime connections absent from auth.log. VIM signature in slack space. Decreasing PIDs. inode mtime 6 hours after last entry.
peirce_expected.thirdness: The body of evidence reveals a deliberate cover-up operation: first exfiltrate, then edit the log to erase the sessions. The precision of the editing (erasing only the nighttime entries, preserving the daytime ones) indicates technical knowledge of syslog format and root access to the server.
